chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ath, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hazrami, from his father who said:

I returned from Makkah, so I met Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) in the Masjid, and he was seated in what is between the grave and the pulpit. So I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! When I go out to Makkah, sometimes a man says to me, 'Circumambulate on my behalf, seven circuits, and pray two cycles.' But I am too preoccupied from that, so when I return, I do not know what I should say to him.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you go to Makkah, so fulfill your rituals, circumambulate seven circuits and pray two cycles, then say, "O Allah! This circumambulation and these two cycles are on behalf of my father and my mother, and on behalf of my wife, and on behalf of my children, and on behalf of my protectors, and on behalf of the entirety of the people of my city, their free ones, and their slaves, and their white ones, and their black ones."'
So you would not be saying to the man, 'I have performed a circumambulation on your behalf, and prayed two cycles on your behalf,' except that you would be truthful (in saying that).
So you would not be saying to the man, 'I conveyed the greetings to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family),' except that you would be truthful (in saying that).
ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a request to perform Hajj or prayer on behalf of another person when busy?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of *Tawassul* (seeking means) and the validity of dedicating the spiritual reward of one's obligatory acts to others, rather than performing the physical rituals *in loco* for them. Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) provides a practical liturgical formula, instructing the narrator to perform his own Tawaf and prayers while explicitly invoking the deceased or specific individual as the recipient of the *Salam* and reward, thus satisfying the social obligation truthfully. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of the community (*Ummah*) where the merit of the living can benefit the dead or absent relatives.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Ash’as, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Hazramy, from his father who said,

‘I returned from Makkah, so I met Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> in the Masjid, and he<sup>asws</sup> was seated in what is between the grave and the Pulpit (of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>). So I said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! When I go out to Makkah, sometimes the man says to me, ‘Circumambulate on my behalf, seven (circuits), and Pray two Cycles’. But, I am too pre-occupied from that, so when I return, I do not know what I should be saying to him’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you go to Makkah, so fulfil your rituals, circumambulate seven (circuits) and Pray two Cycles, then say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! This circumambulation, and these two Cycles (of Prayer) are no behalf of my father and my mother, and on behalf of my wife, and on behalf of my children, and of behalf of my protectors, and on behalf of the entirety of the people of my city, their free ones, and their slaves, and their white ones, and their black ones’.
So you would not be saying to the man, ‘I have performed a circumambulation on your behalf, and Prayed two Cycles on your behalf’, except that you would be truthful (in saying that).

So when you go to the grave of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, fulfil what is Obligatory upon you. Pray two Cycles, then pause by the head of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, then say, ‘Greetings be upon you<sup>saww</sup>, O Prophet<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, from my father and my mother, and my wife, and my children, and the entirety of the people of my city, their free ones, and they slaves, and their white ones, and their black ones’. So you would not be saying to the man, ‘I conveyed the greetings to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’, except that you would be truthful (in saying that)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain persons of our people from Ali ibn Muhammad al- Ash‘ath from Ibrahim al-Hadramiy from his father who has said the following:

“I once returned from Makkah and met abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the Masjid sitting between the pulpit and the grave. I said, ‘O child of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, when I go out to Makkah, perhaps a man asks me to perform a Tawaf and two Rak‘at Salat (prayer) for him, but I become busy and cannot do so. When I return I do not know what to say to him.

He (the Imam) said, ‘When you go to Makkah and complete the acts, perform a Tawaf and two Rak‘at Salat (prayer). Then say, ‘O Lord, this Tawaf and these two Rak‘at are for my father, mother, wife, children, my protectors, and for all of the people of my city, the free and slaves, white and black.’
Thereafter if you say to a man that you have performed Tawaf and two Rak‘at Salat (prayer) for him, you will be truthful.

When you come to the grave of the Holy prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to your cause, after completing what is obligatory upon you, perform two Rak‘at Salat (prayer). Then stand near the head of the Holy prophet, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and say, ‘I offer you greeting of peace, O the Holy prophet of Allah. I do this for my father, mother, wife, children, all of my protectors, all people of my city, the free ones, the slaves, the white and black ones.’ Thereafter if you say to a man that you have offered greeting of peace to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, for him, you have remained truthful.’”
